text: [mechanism] Spawning a task moves its backlog item to In flight in the same run, and refuses when this home has no item for the work.

sources.quote: the spawn itself moves the work item to In flight and refuses rather than dispatching work this home has no item for

text: [mechanism] Under the backlog gate, dispatch accepts only an unheld, unblocked Queued or In flight item; any other item is refused before an endpoint or local copy exists.

sources.quote: dispatch accepts only an unheld, unblocked Queued or In flight item in this home
refused before any endpoint or local copy is created

text: [mechanism] When a project declares a worker capacity and every place is held, the spawn script prints a deferred line and exits 75 before it renders a brief or creates an endpoint, worktree, record or backlog move; the item stays queued. A place is freed when a worker records its ready PR or is cleaned up.

sources.quote: exits 75 before any brief
was not launched and its backlog item stays queued
dispatch it again once one of them records its ready PR or is cleaned up

text: [mechanism] An unreadable capacity declaration makes the spawn refuse with exit 1 instead of guessing the limit.

sources.quote: spawn refused: the project capacity declaration is unreadable

text: [prose-only] Isolated work is dispatched at once with no concurrency cap; only a declared project capacity bounds it. The rule is an instruction to the agent.

sources.quote: dispatch isolated work immediately with no concurrency cap

text: [prose-only] Work is serialized only for a true dependency, shared mutable external state or a similar concrete condition; same-file editing alone is not enough. No code enforces this choice.

sources.quote: Serialize only for a true semantic dependency

text: [mechanism] A spawn that cannot take the shared project lock exits 1 and does not wait.

sources.quote: refusing to race it

text: [mechanism] Worktree allocation and return serialize on one project lock per machine-local firstmate tree.

sources.quote: Allocation and return serialize on one project lock per machine-local Firstmate tree

text: [prose-only] A deferred item is dispatched again by the agent when capacity frees, after every teardown and heartbeat. The cited text states no count or limit on how often an item may be deferred.

sources.quote: Re-evaluate queued work after every teardown and heartbeat
dispatch it again once one of them records its ready PR or is cleaned up

text: [mechanism] A ship's done report is refused while the named head exists only in the worker's disposable copy; the crew-state, PR-check and secondmate publisher call the same gate.

sources.quote: refuses a ship `done:` while that head exists only in the worker's disposable copy

text: [prose-only] After a PR or ready branch exists, the task waits for the configured merge authority; with yolo off the captain approves every PR merge and local-only landing. The cited text sets no deadline for the captain.

sources.quote: then waits for the configured merge authority
with it off, the captain approves every PR merge and every local-only landing

text: [mechanism] Teardown of a ship worktree is fail-closed: a dirty worktree refuses, and committed work must be landed before the worktree is returned.

sources.quote: Teardown is fail-closed for ship worktrees: dirty worktrees refuse

text: [mechanism] Removing a task's record and landing its backlog close are one step under the task's own lock, and the script reports success only after both. Nothing else, such as a later agent turn or a printed reminder, carries the pairing.

sources.quote: Removing state/<id>.meta and landing the backlog transition are one step, not
Nothing else - not a later agent turn, not a printed reminder - is

text: [mechanism] A teardown whose backlog close fails is fatal and loud, keeps its pending-close record, and is retried by the next session start. The cited header states no count or limit on those retries.

sources.quote: preserves its pending-close record
is retried by the next session start

text: [mechanism] The bootstrap script replays whatever a crash left behind, for this home only, and the writer and the replay share one validator for the pending-close record.

sources.quote: replays whatever a crash left behind, THIS HOME ONLY
The writer and replay share one complete-record validator

text: [mechanism] A replay of a pending close can end incomplete: its result is one of closed, closed_incomplete, retained, retained_incomplete, answered, stale or noop.

sources.quote: closed | closed_incomplete | retained |

text: [prose-only] On a stale wake the agent inspects the recorded endpoint and loads the stuck-worker recovery procedure for a stopped, looping, confused or unresponsive worker. The choice to recover is the agent's.

sources.quote: inspect the recorded endpoint and load `stuck-crewmate-recovery` for a stopped, looping, confused, or unresponsive worker

text: [mechanism] The relaunch verb replaces the running agent with a new one in the same worktree, and a ship or scout relaunch requires a note that is appended to the instructions the new agent reads.

sources.quote: Replace the running agent with a new one in the same worktree
the note is appended to the instructions it reads

text: [mechanism] A relaunch that fails after the old agent was stopped restores the prior durable record and reports that no agent is running.

sources.quote: restores the prior durable record

text: [prose-only] No bound on relaunches was found. The only retry count in the control script's header (searched for attempt, max and retries) is for the Enter key of the exit command, so nothing in code limits how often one task is relaunched.

sources.quote: Enter retries for the exit command (3)

text: [prose-only] Choosing the harness for a dispatch is the agent's judgment; the scripts validate the shape but do not parse task intent or match the rules.

sources.quote: they do not parse task intent, match natural-language rules, or own array selection

text: [mechanism] A spawn must resolve an isolated task worktree distinct from the primary checkout; a failed isolation assertion stops the task.

sources.quote: a failed isolation assertion stops the task
